items.title: 68099_Erskine Hawkins oral history interview
items.q: He taught me how to drive on the road. His name was Fitzgerald. I'll never forget it. Ed Fitzgerald, an Irishman.

ctx.x: But, I didn't mind driving. I just wanted it when I needed the car to go somewhere. I didn't want to take the bus or this and that. You know?

So, the bus driver used to say just make 50 miles an hour steady. And I was out there doing 60 and 70 and I told myself I was gonna get there in time before the band got there? And you, and when I had to stop for a light and he was doing 50 miles, he was behind me. He taught me how to drive on the road. His name was Fitzgerald. I'll never forget it. Ed Fitzgerald, an Irishman. He was beautiful. A senior citizen. He drove me all the way from Texas to New York. I don't know how he did it. Three thousand miles.
That's when I was telling you about the Savoy Ballroom when the Golden Gate was opening up. He was the driver. I'll never forget him. But, he got us there for us to get on that band stand in time.
